item.title: Over 1,000 children are buried at juvenile detention centers nationwide
item.description: Researchers uncovered the graves of more than 1,000 children next to juvenile detention facilities in 29 states. At one Maryland gravesite, 230 Black boys are buried.
item.content:encoded:
Researchers uncovered the graves of more than 1,000 children next to juvenile detention facilities in 29 states. At one Maryland gravesite, 230 Black boys are buried.

(Image credit: Tyrone Turner/WAMU for NPR)

item.title: Deep in Appalachia, a rail-to-trail project builds bipartisan support for a bridge
item.description: The Trump administration has been hostile to federal spending on bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure. But there's bipartisan support for a multiuse trail that would connect Ohio and West Virginia.

item.title: Carpetbagger allegation, misplaced valor make Nevada's safe red House seat competitive
item.description: Northern Nevada has a reliably red congressional seat, represented by a Republican since it was drawn in the early 1980s. A complicated candidate and a potential blue wave this year could change that.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: 5 things civil rights data says about public schools
item.description: The federal Civil Rights Data Collection, for the first time in decades, tells us about the teacher workforce and reminds us racial disparities are still stark in American public schools.

item.title: Cornell students plan sit-in to protest handling of former student's rape allegations
item.description: Former U.S. Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates will lead an independent inquiry into Cornell's handling of a former student's rape allegations. Students are preparing for a sit-in Wednesday.

item.title: Former Tennessee prisons chief also oversaw botched executions in Arizona
item.description: Before Tennessee's prisons chief stepped down in the aftermath of a horrific failed execution, he oversaw botched executions in Arizona. A review of protocols there spelled out serious issues.

item.title: Trump approves execution by firing squad for 2009 Fort Hood shooter
item.description: President Trump has approved an execution by firing squad for the former Army psychiatrist who opened fire and killed 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009.

item.title: Former CIA official accused of stealing $40M in gold bars pleads guilty
item.description: A former senior CIA official pleaded guilty Tuesday to a charge that he abused his position to enrich himself by acquiring Florida real estate and hundreds of gold bars worth over $40 million.

item.title: Trump says Fort Hood shooter can be executed by firing squad
item.description: The last time the U.S. military held an execution was in 1961, by hanging. The last military execution by firing squad was in 1945, when an American soldier was shot for desertion in World War II.
